svg.desc: A position-bias test. The same pair of answers is shown to an LLM judge twice: first with the correct answer X in slot A, then with it in slot B. The judge answers A both times, so it picked the correct answer once and the corrupted one once: the position decided. The position-bias rate is the share of pairs that get the same letter in both orders.

svg.text: Debias: average the log-prob margin log P(A) − log P(B) for each candidate over its two positions.

svg.text: The notebook's 0.5B judge said “A” every time (rate 1.00); debiased, it preferred the correct answer in 75% of pairs.
